cluster_name: Trump-Xi White House summit yields $30B tariff deal and AI safety channel
tldr: The headline layer across 35 outlets and 19 countries divides almost cleanly into two registers: a concrete-deliverable cluster advertising the $30 billion tariff cut and AI communication channel, and a Western-dominated meta-commentary cluster foregrounding pageantry, personal chemistry, and the absence of substantive breakthrough. Chinese state media headlines stand entirely apart, advertising the summit as an exercise in 'dynamic stability' through 'head-of-state diplomacy' — vocabulary absent from every other outlet in the corpus — while HKFP and Asia Times are the only outlets whose titles explicitly flag Xi's red lines on Taiwan and Iran.
event_summary: Xi Jinping visited Washington September 24–26, 2026, meeting Trump at the White House; the two sides agreed to tariff cuts on $30 billion in non-sensitive goods, an AI safety communication channel, and Chinese coal purchases from the US.

outlet_isolation_top.note: China bucket most isolated at headline level; both CGTN titles use 'dynamic stability' and 'head-of-state diplomacy' vocabulary with no deal specifics — an advertised framing absent from every other outlet in the corpus

Mexico bucket second-most isolated; only Spanish-language outlet in the corpus, framing via 'pactan' and 'aranceles' register, entirely absent the 'no-breakthrough' meta-commentary that clusters in anglophone titles

Russia bucket third-most isolated; RT leads with AI cooperation framing ('discuss AI cooperation', 'establish AI hotline') while omitting Taiwan, Iran, and the skeptical-assessment angle prominent elsewhere

single_outlet_findings.finding: Both CGTN headlines advertise the visit entirely as a process achievement ('Head-of-state diplomacy underpins dynamic stability of China-US ties', ''Respect, fairness, reciprocity' key to China-US strategic stability') — the only titles in the corpus to frame the summit without naming a single concrete outcome, advertising a relationship narrative that no other outlet's homepage mirrors.

The only headline in the corpus to reduce the AI pact to a terminological joke — 'Trump And Xi Found Common Ground On AI: Its Name' — framing the 'super intelligence' dialogue as a mere branding exercise and marking the widest headline-layer skepticism on the AI outcome within the US press.

The only headline to frame Trump's welcome as authoritarian-solidarity theater ('Trump swoons over strongman soulmate Xi – are you feeling jealous, Vladimir?'), a register absent from every other outlet's title including the full UK press, and the starkest example of a political-character frame surfacing at headline level rather than being buried in opinion body text.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, this summit is advertised primarily as two concrete outputs — a $30 billion tariff cut and an AI safety channel — but a substantial bloc of Western and Asia-Pacific commentary outlets explicitly tell readers in the title itself that the event produced more ceremony than substance. Chinese state media CGTN diverges most sharply, framing the visit entirely through 'dynamic stability' and 'head-of-state diplomacy' vocabulary absent from every other outlet's homepage. The Taiwan dimension — extensively covered in body text — surfaces in only a handful of titles concentrated in pro-DPP and Japanese outlets, rendering it nearly invisible at the global headline layer.
